en: So if I were to explain JEV to you, I would go to this table on the TypeSafe blog post announcing JEV, and it basically compares normal LLMs on the left, JEV style LLMs on the right.
zh: 所以如果我要向你解释 JEV,我会去看 TypeSafe 发布 JEV 的那篇博客文章上的这张表,它基本上把普通 LLM 放在左边,JEV 风格的 LLM 放在右边进行比较。

speaker: Unknown
en: Both take in unstructured data as inputs.
zh: 两者都接收非结构化数据作为输入。

speaker: Unknown
en: Both take in text as inputs.
zh: 两者都接收文本作为输入。

speaker: Unknown
en: Jev does not take in images, but it takes in text, and it takes in text descriptions of images if you really need to get there.
zh: Jev 不接收图像,但它接收文本,如果你真的需要的话,它也接收图像的文本描述。

speaker: Unknown
en: The outputs, though, are very different.
zh: 不过输出就非常不同了。

speaker: Unknown
en: With the standard LLMs that you're used to working with, you are getting strings and generated text out.
zh: 用你熟悉的那些标准 LLM,你得到的是字符串和生成的文本。

speaker: Unknown
en: Text in, text out.
zh: 文本进,文本出。

speaker: Unknown
en: With Jev, you're getting text in, type safe values out.
zh: 用 Jev,你是文本进,类型安全的值出。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what I mean by type safe values is these are values that are predefined that then Jev picks from and selects and returns to you.
zh: 我说的类型安全的值是指,这些是预先定义好的值,然后 Jev 从中挑选、选择并返回给你。

speaker: Unknown
en: We will show you what those values are, but essentially they're like, it's this or that, it's yes or no, it's one through 10.
zh: 我们会给你看那些值是什么,但基本上就是,是这个或那个,是或否,一到十。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like it's pretty simple.
zh: 就是很简单。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now it sounds simple, but it is incredibly powerful when you put it against the right problem.
zh: 现在听起来很简单,但当你把它用在合适的问题上时,它强大得不可思议。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other thing that you will notice about Jeff is it is cheap AF and it is fast AF.
zh: 关于 Jeff 你会注意到的另一件事是,它便宜得要命,而且快得要命。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you look at the current cost of input and output tokens, it can be pennies to tens or hundreds of dollars per million output tokens.
zh: 所以如果你看看目前输入和输出 tokens 的成本,其他模型可能是每百万输出 tokens 几美分到几十甚至几百美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: JEV only charges you on input tokens because it barely outputs anything.
zh: JEV 只按输入 tokens 收费,因为它几乎什么都不输出。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it is four cents per million input tokens.
zh: 而且它是每百万输入 tokens 四美分。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is like dirt, freaking cheap.
zh: 便宜得像 dirt 一样,真的便宜到离谱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And because they output basically nothing, they don't even charge you.
zh: 而且因为它们基本什么都不输出,他们甚至不收你的费。

speaker: Unknown
en: For output tokens, whereas the standard LLMs are going to charge you tons for the output tokens.
zh: 至于输出 token,标准 LLM 会在输出 token 上收你很多钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I'll go into use cases, which is how you would use like a standard LLM versus why you would use JEV.
zh: 然后我会讲使用场景，也就是你会怎么用标准 LLM,以及为什么要用 JEV。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, standard LLMs, chatbots, where you want text in, you want text out.
zh: 你知道，标准 LLM、聊天机器人，是你想要文本进、文本出。

speaker: Unknown
en: Coding, where you want, you know, code to be produced.
zh: 写代码，是你想要生成代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's great for things where you need stuff generated.
zh: 所以它很适合需要生成内容的场景。

speaker: Unknown
en: But JEV is really great for making decisions.
zh: 但 JEV 真正擅长的是做决策。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's ultimately what you've been calling this.
zh: 这就是为什么大家给它起的这个名字。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like a decision model.
zh: 它就像一个决策模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you give it a decision and it makes a decision.
zh: 所以你给它一个决策，它就做出一个决策。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's high agency, I would say.
zh: 我会说它有很高的主观能动性。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you need smart if statements, should I go left or right?
zh: 所以如果你需要聪明的 if 语句，我该往左还是往右？

speaker: Unknown
en: If it's good, put it to this person.
zh: 如果是好的，交给这个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: If it's bad, send it to support.
zh: 如果是坏的，转给客服支持。

speaker: Unknown
en: All that kind of stuff Jeff is really good at.
zh: 这类事情 Jeff 都非常擅长。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really good at classifying data.
zh: 它非常擅长给数据分类。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a lot of what I'm going to talk to you about today.
zh: 这也是我今天要讲的大量内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really good at real time.
zh: 它非常擅长实时场景。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it is fast, fast, fast.
zh: 所以它很快、很快、非常快。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you can put an LLM in a real time loop in a way that was not performant enough with these other models.
zh: 所以你可以把一个 LLM 放进实时循环里，用其他模型的话性能是不够的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I would highly recommend if you're going to use Jev, go to their docs.

speaker: Unknown
en: The two places that I'm using the most are the primitives.
zh: 我用得最多的两个地方是 primitives。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what it returns, and then I use some of the patterns in cookbooks.
zh: 也就是它返回什么，然后我用了一些 cookbooks 里的模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what will Jev return to you?
zh: 那么 Jev 会返回给你什么？

speaker: Unknown

zh: 它基本上会返回三种东西之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: It will return a choice, which means you can give it text.
zh: 它会返回一个 choice,意思是你可以给它文本。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can give it a list of choices and it will pick a choice.
zh: 你可以给它一个选项列表，它会挑选一个选项。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if my question is, what should I wear on this date?
zh: 所以如果我的问题是，这个约会我该穿什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And my choice is a dress, jeans, workout clothes, ski gear, or nothing.
zh: 我的选项是连衣裙、牛仔裤、运动服、滑雪装备，或者什么都不穿。

speaker: Unknown
en: It'll like maybe pick the dress, right?

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that is choice.
zh: 这就是 choice。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I select score, it's going to say like, how severe is this?

speaker: Unknown
en: Or on a score from one to five, what it is.

speaker: Unknown
en: This is really good for severity rankings.
zh: 这对严重程度排序非常有用。

speaker: Unknown
en: So say the example here is a great one, which is like, if you get a bug, you want to rank it like cosmetic, broken or blocking, Jev will triage that bug and give it a score.

speaker: Unknown
en: And then finally, there's a null.
zh: 最后，还有 null。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: So if the answer to a question is yes or no, is Claire a podcaster?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's going to give you like a 99% null because there's a 99% chance.

speaker: Unknown
en: That I am a podcaster.
zh: 我是一个播客主持人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is how, you know, you would think about the three things that can return.
zh: 所以这就是，你知道的，你可以怎么理解它能返回的三种东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, very simple.
zh: 再说一遍，非常简单。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you've been a software engineer, this is like 90% of software engineering is like doing these things, returning a choice, scoring something, routing, saying yes or no.
zh: 但如果你当过软件工程师，软件工程 90% 的工作就是做这些事情，返回一个选择、给某样东西打分、路由、说是或否。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it is just so, so, so powerful.
zh: 所以它就是这么、这么、这么强大。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the number one thing I have been using it for is classification of vast sets of unstructured data that would have been annoying to classify but is very high value.

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm going to show you those use cases and hopefully this will inspire you about how you can use JEV.

en: Okay, so I'm going to pull up Codex and show you like two or three examples that are super simple to run, incredibly cheap and incredibly powerful.

speaker: Unknown
en: This is one CTOs, VPs of product, you know, chief product officers, listen up.

speaker: Unknown
en: This is the one that three years ago I would have paid truly $100,000 for.

speaker: Unknown
en: So what I had Jev do is look at thousands of PRs.
zh: 所以我让 Jev 做的是查看数千个 PR。

speaker: Unknown
en: I got PRs.

speaker: Unknown
en: I have connection to GitHub, pull every single PR.
zh: 我连接了 GitHub,把每一个 PR 都拉取下来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then what I had it do, which would have been so impractical in the past, is I said, categorize all the PRs.
zh: 然后我让它做的事情——在过去这是极不现实的——是,我说,把所有 PR 分类。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so use Jev to do pairwise relations.
zh: 于是用 Jev 来做两两配对的关系判断。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this is something that I found Jev is really good at is compare like PRA to PRB and say, are you the same?
zh: 这是我发现 Jev 真正擅长的事情,就是比较 PR A 和 PR B,然后问,你们是同一个吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you working on the same thematic area or not?
zh: 你们是否在处理同一个主题领域?

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, Jev's not going to tell you what the thematic area is unless you give it choices.
zh: 再说一次,Jev 不会告诉你主题领域是什么,除非你给它选项。

speaker: Unknown
en: Instead, it's going to say like, yes, these two are related or no, they're not.
zh: 相反,它只会说,比如,是的,这两个相关,或者不,它们不相关。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I've been doing this a lot where I'm taking vast amounts of data and I'm saying like, yes, related, not related, yes, related, not related.
zh: 我经常这么做,拿大量数据,然后说,是的,相关,不,不相关,是的,相关,不,不相关。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's doing clustering, which I find very, very useful.
zh: 它在做聚类,我觉得这非常有用。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I create these clusters of data sets and that's what Jev did.
zh: 所以我创建了这些数据集聚类,这就是 Jev 做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I used a really cheap model.
zh: 然后我用了一个非常便宜的模型。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: It cost me 1.1 cent.
zh: 花了我 1.1 美分。

speaker: Unknown
en: I guess they wouldn't round down that 0.1 penny.
zh: 我猜他们不愿意把那 0.1 美分抹掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can see here, it lets me see how much of my work is related to maintenance, content, tools, site and conversion services, or docs.
zh: 你可以在这里看到,它让我看到我的工作有多少与维护、内容、工具、网站和转化服务或文档相关。

speaker: Unknown
en: Super useful.
zh: 非常有用。

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, it ran very, very, very fast and very cheap, but then I ran it on my ChatPRD app, which has about 2,000 PRs on it to date in this calendar year.
zh: 再说一次,它跑得非常非常快、非常便宜,但接着我在我的 ChatPRD 应用上运行,今年日历年度它大约有 2,000 个 PR。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because it has a lot more PRs, it cost me a lot more money, and by a lot more money, I mean nine whole cents.
zh: 因为它的 PR 多得多,所以花的钱也多得多,所谓多得多,我是指整整 9 美分。

speaker: Unknown
en: It cost me nine cents to do this.
zh: 做这件事花了我 9 美分。

speaker: Unknown
en: It took probably about two minutes.
zh: 大概花了两分钟。

speaker: Unknown
en: What it did is it analyzed 1,700 PRs.
zh: 它做的是分析了 1,700 个 PR。

speaker: Unknown
en: It found 17,000 pairs in those PRs of things that could be matched, and then the themes were labeled by Gemini Flashlight, and it pulled all of the data out.
zh: 它在这些 PR 中找到了 17,000 对可以匹配的内容,然后主题由 Gemini Flashlight 标注,它把所有数据都提取出来了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, again,
zh: 我是说,再说一次,

speaker: Unknown
en: CTOs, CEOs, I know you're asked this by the board and by your team and by your boss all the time.
zh: CTO 们、CEO 们,我知道董事会、你的团队和你的老板总是问你们这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: What percentage of work is going to what initiatives?
zh: 有多少百分比的工作投入到哪些计划?

speaker: Unknown
en: Tell me the percentage to tech debt.
zh: 告诉我投入到技术债务的百分比。

speaker: Unknown
en: Tell me the percentage to this product or that product.
zh: 告诉我投入到这个产品或那个产品的百分比。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can see here, it got down, it excluded our docs PRs because those are completely separate.
zh: 你可以在这里看到,它排除了我们的文档 PR,因为那些是完全独立的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Almost 30% of the effort, the PRs that we do at ChatPRD, around platform security and infrastructure.
zh: 在 ChatPRD 我们所做的 PR 中,将近 30% 的精力投入到平台安全和基础设施。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm being a good citizen and investing in security performance and infrastructure.

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, of course, because we're a chatbot, a conversational AI reliability, and then some product areas that we invest in are like data and integrations, document editing, and prototyping, which is new.

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this was so cheap, so fast.

speaker: Unknown
en: It is accurate.

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I can just tell you, yes, this is where we're investing our time.

en: And you can even see as we invest more in different things over the last couple of months, it goes up.
